startOfReception.title: Welcome to Wren Phonics
body: Welcome to Reception! Over the next few weeks your child will start daily phonics sessions using Wren Phonics, a complete programme for teaching reading and spelling.

Phonics teaches children to read by matching the sounds in words (phonemes) to the letters that spell them (graphemes), then blending those sounds together left to right to read the whole word — and segmenting a word into its sounds to spell it, which is simply blending in reverse.

The first week is an "Introduction" week: games, rhymes and listening activities that tune children’s ears in to sounds, with no letters at all yet. Letters begin in week two, starting with s, a, t and p — the classic first set that unlocks real words fastest.

Every sound is taught as a PURE sound — a quick, clipped "t", never "tuh"; a held "sss", never "suh". If you are ever unsure how a sound should sound, ask your child’s teacher rather than guessing — getting this right really does make blending easier.

Once your child has a handful of sounds, they will bring home their first Wren Phonics reading book, matched exactly to what they have been taught so far so they can read it independently rather than guess. A separate letter explains the TWO kinds of book your child will bring home.

You will also receive a reading-record booklet each half-term, with that half-term’s sounds and tricky words, space to log reading at home, and tips for listening to your child read (overleaf in the booklet, and summarised here too).
Thank you for reading with your child at home — little and often, with lots of praise for their effort, makes a real difference.
startOfReception.tipsHeading: A few tips for reading together

twoBooks.title: Your child’s two reading books
body: From now on your child may bring home two different kinds of book, and it helps to know they are used quite differently.

The READING PRACTICE book is matched exactly to the sounds and tricky words your child has been taught so far in school. It is for your child to read to YOU, independently, sounding out every word — nothing in it should need to be guessed from the picture. We ask you to read the SAME book three times across the week (your child’s teacher will say which book and which week) — the first read is hard decoding work, and each re-read lets your child read a little more smoothly and with more expression, which is exactly the point, not a sign of being stuck.

The SHARING book is chosen much more freely — a library book, a book from home, anything that catches your child’s interest — and is read WITH an adult, for enjoyment. You do most of the reading here; this book is about vocabulary, story and the sheer pleasure of books, not about independent decoding, and it is never assessed against the phonics schedule.

Both matter, and both are "reading" — just for different reasons. If your child’s reading practice book looks very short and simple, that is because it deliberately only uses what has been taught so far; it will grow as the taught code grows.

howToListen: Give them time to work out a word sound-by-sound before jumping in to help.
If they get stuck, prompt with "what’s the first sound?" rather than saying the word for them.
A tricky word they haven’t been taught yet is fine to simply tell them, rather than letting them guess from the picture.
Praise the effort of sounding out, not just getting a word right first try.
Little and often beats one long session — a few minutes most days is plenty.
Let them re-read the same book more than once. That is not a sign they are "stuck" — it is exactly what builds fluent, confident reading.
